g.text: Child work was once common, and has declined sharply

text.style: font-size: 11.52px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #5b5b5b

g.text: Share of children recorded as working, from population censuses and other national records. Each series is labeled

text.style: font-size: 11.52px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #5b5b5b

g.text: with the country, the age group and the sex it covers.

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #858585

g.text: Note: These estimates come from a dozen different studies and are not strictly comparable: the age group, the sex covered and what counts as work all

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #858585

g.text: vary. Census counts also understate children's work, particularly unpaid work at home. The two world series in grey are ILO estimates rather than census

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #858585

g.text: counts; Toniolo and Vecchi find the 1950-1995 series far too high for Italy.

text.style: font-size: 8.64px; font-family: 'Lato', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #858585

g.text: Data source: Basu (1999); Carter and Sutch (1996); Cunningham and Viazzo (1996); Heywood (1988); International Labour Organization and UNICEF
